newsitem.title: INDIA: India's rulers to decide on oil soon - Chidambaram.
newsitem.headline: India's rulers to decide on oil soon - Chidambaram.

text.p: Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said on Saturday that the ruling United Front will decide whether to raise the prices of domestic petroleum products at the coalition's next meeting.
The United Front is scheduled to take up the issue on June 27.
"We will reach a decision collectively next time," the finance minister told a news conference in the capital.
Asked how much longer the government could wait before deciding whether to raise the prices of some petroleum products, Chidambaram said: "Not very long. A solution has to be found."

At its last meeting on June 16, the 15-party United Front postponed a decision on whether to raise prices to plug the government's mounting debt to state oil companies, estimated at 155 billion rupees ($4.3 billion) at the end of March.
Leftwing parties in Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's alliance have strongly opposed any price increase.
On Wednesday, Petroleum Minister Janeshwar Mishra was quoted as saying the government would raise the prices of petroleum products by the end of June, and the increase would be "almost negligible".
